title: Gil Evans and Miles Davis
summary: He says Miles insisted on Gil Evans as arranger and Gil was serene and a genius.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: You also recorded with Gil on his dates.

Oh yeah, “Out of the Cool” and you know, Charlie Persip was one of his main drummers too. He played in a lot of Gil’s record sessions. One that I was there, and all I could do was rattle the tambourine. It was just a lot of fun; that was the thing about Gil Evans, he had a sense of humor.
Was the dynamic like between Gil and Miles when you observed them in a studio and performance?

Well Miles wouldn’t even hear of another arranger other than Gil Evans. They were very close; they were close personal friends. You know, Miles would get in trouble or something and he’d call up Gil and Gil would talk to him like a father. And he was like that, Gil was so serene and he kept his life that way. I never heard him raise his voice and he was a genius as an arranger. There was nobody any better than that.
